extracted.intended_audience: chemical indexers, patent/chemical information specialists, and database searchers using the Derwent Chemical Index
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and code-assigning rules for indexing chemical structures (functional groups, bonds, oxo/thioxo, heteroatom bonds, valencies, tautomers, halogens) in the Derwent Chemical Index. Covers Parts H:, J:, K:, and L: with examples and time-range/precursor-code notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: H72: Non-cyclic >C=C< group present
rubrics_metrics.description: Set H72 codes describe non-cyclic >C=C< groups present with subsets H720 through H725 (exocyclic, one >C=C< not exocyclic, two unconjugated, three or more unconjugated, two conjugated, three or more conjugated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: (1) H720 is assigned to >C=C< groups where one C is a ring member or where the two C atoms are members of different rings. (2) Conjugation of double bonds does not include double bonds in rings; conjugation continues through one single bond in a ring, so two exocyclic >C=C< groups on adjacent ring C atoms are coded as two conjugated double bonds (assign H720 and H724). (3) If conjugated and unconjugated double bonds exist in the same structure, code them separately (e.g., for three double bonds with two conjugated, assign H721 and H724). (4) Exocyclic >C=C< groups are not counted when applying H721, H722, or H723. Examples illustrate combinations (e.g. CH2=CH-CH=CH-CH2- => H721, H724).

rubrics_metrics.name: H73: Acetylinic bonds present
rubrics_metrics.description: Set H73 codes indicate presence and multiplicity/location of -C#C- (acetylinic) bonds: H730 (one or more -C#C- groups present in a ring), H731 (one non-cyclic -C#C- group present), H732 (two or more non-cyclic -C#C- groups present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to distinguish ring vs non-ring acetylinic bonds and multiplicity; examples provided (structures annotated with H73 subset codes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Part J scope: common functional groups with >C=O or >C=S
rubrics_metrics.description: Part J codes refer to common functional groups containing a carbonyl (C=O) or thionyl (C=S) group; some groups with carbonyl/thionyl are coded elsewhere (Parts K: and L:) and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be coded in Part J, the carbonyl (or thionyl) side of the functional group must be directly bonded to H or C. Code definitions include the S-analogue name in parentheses (e.g., 'Ester (thioester)'). Symbol definitions specific to Part J (T, T', U, R, X, Y) are provided to interpret code definitions. Exception: oxo and thioxo groups bonded to ring C atoms are coded in Set J5: even if further bonded only to heteroatoms (O,S,Se,Te,N,halogen).

rubrics_metrics.name: Part J: symbol definitions (T, T', U, R, X, Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Symbols in Part J code definitions represent element classes: T = O, S, Se, or Te (valency II); T' = S, Se, or Te (valency IV or more); U = O, S, Se, Te, or N; R = C or H; X = halogen (F, Cl, Br, I); Y = O, S, Se, Te, N, or halogen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These symbol definitions may vary independently when appearing more than once in a fragment; they are used throughout Part J definitions and guide when additional specificity codes are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Groups NOT coded in Part J
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of specific structural motifs that are not coded in Part J and the Part/Subset used instead (examples include non-ring U-C(=T)-U coded in L550; N-C(=O)-N coded in L570; -C(=T)-U-C(=T)- coded in L520; -R-C(=T')-R coded in L951; -R-C(=T)-S-Y coded in L951; -R-C(=T)-O-X coded in L951).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the indicated Part L codes for these arrangements instead of Part J codes; examples and illustrations provided. Choosing the correct code part is discussed elsewhere (see 'Guidelines For Choosing Applicable Functional Group Codes').

rubrics_metrics.name: Groups coded in Part J despite appearing in other Parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain groups are coded in Part J (with specified examples), including R-C(=T')-U- (same as SII analogue), -C-C(=SIV=O)-S-, R-C(=T)-NO2 (amide-like), R-C(=T)-O-O-R (peroxyester analogues), and others where Part J codes apply and sometimes additional K/L codes also apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some of these groups are also indexed in Parts K: or L: (e.g., some peroxyesters also receive K910). The manual lists examples and cross-references (also notes some groups are additionally indexed in Part K or L).

rubrics_metrics.name: J0: Number of carboxylic acid, ester, and amide groups present
rubrics_metrics.description: Set J0 provides codes for the count of carboxylic acid, ester, and amide groups present: J011 (one), J012 (two), J013 (three), J014 (four or more).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: thiocarboxylic acid, thioester, and thioamide groups are not counted when applying Set J0 codes. Prior to 1981, some additional group types were also assigned to J0 subsets; time-range/precursor differences are documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: J1: Carboxylic acid and thiocarboxylic acid coding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Set J1 codes carboxylic acid and thiocarboxylic acid groups (subsets J11..J17, etc.) and J19 for thiocarboxylic acid groups bonded to specific atom types (heterocyclic, aromatic, alicyclic, H/aliphatic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be coded in Set J1, the acid group must be bonded to H or C. Salts of carboxylic/thiocarboxylic acids are assigned the same J1 code as the parent acid. Peroxyacids are assigned the same code as the corresponding carboxylic acid and also receive K910. Thiocarboxylic acid groups are not coded in Sets J11..J17 (they have separate J19 subsets).

rubrics_metrics.name: J2: Ester (thioester) coding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Set J2 covers esters and thioesters, with subsets distinguishing bonding to heterocyclic/aromatic/alicyclic/H/aliphatic atoms and multiplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key rules: (1) Thioesters receive the same J2 code as oxygen analogues plus J290 ('Thioester present'). (2) Esters are coded according to guidelines for non-symmetrical functional groups. (3) To be coded in Set J2, the carbonyl (thionyl) group of the ester must be directly bonded to H or C. (4) Peroxyesters are assigned the same code as the corresponding ester and additionally K910. (5) J2 codes apply to esters of hydroxylamines but not to thioesters of hydroxylamines. (6) Groups R-C(=T)-T-C=N- and R-C(=T)-T-C(N) are coded in J2 provided the -T- atom does not have valency IV or VI. (7) Certain related groups are coded in L520, not J2 (e.g., R-C(=T)-O-Y' with Y' = S, Se, Te or halogen).

rubrics_metrics.name: J21-J27: Ester (thioester) subsets by bonding atom and multiplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Ester/thioester subsets partition esters by where the ester is bonded (via >C=O or via O) to heterocyclic, aromatic, alicyclic, or H/aliphatic carbon and by whether one or two or more such groups are present (e.g., J211 one ester bonded to heterocyclic C via >C=O; J212 two or more).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: J290 flags 'Thioester present' and thioesters also receive the applicable J21..J27 subset code in addition to J290. Examples provided illustrating multi-code assignment (e.g., J241 plus J290).

rubrics_metrics.name: J3: Amide (thioamide) coding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Set J3 codes amides and thioamides with subsets partitioned by bonding to heterocyclic/aromatic/alicyclic/H/aliphatic atoms and whether bonding is via >C=O or via N. Subsets include J31..J37.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thioamides receive the same J3 code as their O-analogues plus J390 ('Thioamide present'). Amides are coded per non-symmetrical functional group rules. J3 codes apply to all R-C(=T)-N groups (R = H or C) except R-C(=T)-N-C(=T) groups which are coded in L53:. Amides of formula R-C(=O)-N(heterocyclic N) are assigned a code based on the R-C(=O) group, not on the heterocyclic N. Examples demonstrate combinations and multi-code assignments (e.g., J321, J371, J390).

rubrics_metrics.name: J4: Aldehyde (thioaldehyde) coding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Set J4 codes aldehydes and thioaldehydes with subsets by bonded atom type (heterocyclic, aromatic, alicyclic, H/aliphatic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be coded in Set J4, the -C(=O)-H (or -C(=S)-H) group can only be bonded to H or C. Thioaldehydes receive the same code as oxygen analogues plus J490. Thioaldehydes where the thionyl S has valency IV or more are coded L570, not J4. Hydrates are assigned the same code as corresponding aldehydes and are not coded L650 or L660.

rubrics_metrics.name: J5: Oxo (=O) and Thioxo (=S) coding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Set J5 covers oxo and thioxo groups with subsets for bonding to heterocyclic, alicyclic, or aliphatic carbon and a J59 subset for thioxo groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes include: (1) Thioxo groups are coded in Subset J59:, not as the oxo analogue in Subsets J51..J58. (2) Aliphatic oxo and thioxo codes (J581,J582,J583,J598) are not used for carbonyl/thionyl groups bonded to O, S, Se, Te, N, or halogen. (3) Oxo/thioxo groups bonded to ring C atoms are coded in Set J5: even if further bonded only to heteroatoms. (4) Keto-enol (thioxo-thiol) tautomerism: code in the keto (thioxo) form unless the enol (thiol) -OH (-SH) is bonded to a fully conjugated carbocyclic ring; then different coding applies. (5) Thioketones where S valency > II are coded in L570, not J5. (6) Oxo groups of quinones are coded in L95:, not in J5. Examples and subset codes J52..J59 given.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule: minimum number of functional group codes and largest fragment preference
rubrics_metrics.description: When coding large structural fragments containing heteroatoms, assign the minimum number of functional group codes that together specify every atom of the group and all linkages. The largest possible fragment is searched at each successive stage even if atoms/bonds are covered by more than one code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can lead to some atoms being covered by multiple codes; examples: -S-S-N< searched as -S-S-Y (K222) and -Y-S-N< (K352) together to leave no ambiguity; >N-N-C(=U) searched as K620 and N-C(=O)U (L110) etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule: if code definition includes variable symbols, add codes identifying the elements
rubrics_metrics.description: If a code's definition contains variable element symbols (T,U,V,W,X,Y,Z), additional functional group codes should usually be used to identify the elements those symbols represent, unless the code definition explicitly states not to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: L620 Note 5 states no additional code should be searched to identify the T atom in S-C(-T)-U; in most other cases further codes from Part K or L are used to fully specify element identities. Examples illustrate when extra codes are or are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precursor (discontinued generic) codes and # marking
rubrics_metrics.description: A code marked with a # on the coding sheet indicates that several current codes have replaced a discontinued less-specific precursor (generic) code; that discontinued code is searchable in time ranges prior to the introduction of the current codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although current examples list only current codes, any available precursor codes should be included in the search strategy for earlier time ranges. Precursor codes and coding time ranges are discussed in the Introduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of poly codes in Parts K: and L:
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts K: and L: frequently use 'poly' codes to indicate that a particular functional group occurs more than once, instead of having separate codes specifying exact multiplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poly codes are applied when a group occurs more than once or when a current code is applicable multiple times (since 1981 behavior differs from earlier years); examples shown for K2, K9 and others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valency coding rules for S, N, halogen (Part C valency codes)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Part K: or L: code does not specify valency for S, N, or halogen, that code can be used for any valency; in certain cases an additional Part C: valency code is assigned (C100/C200/C300 for halogen valency classes; C107/C216/C307, C116/C216/C316 for N and S valencies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valency codes are assigned in addition to K/L codes in cases: (1) halogen with valency II or more; (2) N with valency V or more; (3) all valencies of S; (4) any Part K/L code that is defined for more than one specific valency. The manual provides mappings and examples of when C: valency codes are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halogen identification rules with K/L codes (H60: and C0: usage and time ranges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Symbols X and Y may represent halogens in Part K/L codes; the actual halogen atoms are identified using halogen codes from Subset H60: or Set C0: depending on time range and code color (black vs green codes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: H60 codes were used to identify X atoms in groups coded L330 or L353 from 1963 forward and are included with black codes; C0: codes used to identify X/Y atoms in Parts K/L since 1978 are included with green codes. Example: S-N-Cl coded as K352 and C017 ('Cl'). The 'Coding Rules for Polymers and Halogens' section (page 18) discusses halogen coding more completely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tautomerism affects coding
rubrics_metrics.description: The presence of tautomers can significantly affect the coding of functional groups in Parts K: and L:, and tautomers are discussed in a dedicated 'Tautomerism' section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When keto-enol or thioxo-thiol tautomerism is possible, the structure is usually coded in the keto (thioxo) form unless specific exceptions apply (see J5 notes), e.g., enol -OH bonded to a fully conjugated carbocyclic ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heteroatom-to-metal and heteroatom-to-B/Si/P/As guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Heteroatoms bonded to metals are discussed in Part A ('Guidelines for Coding Compounds Containing Metals'); heteroatoms bonded to B, Si, P, and As are discussed in Part B ('Guidelines for Coding Functional Groups Bonded to B, Si, P, or As').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference guidance: use Parts A/B when heteroatoms are bonded to metals or to B/Si/P/As respectively; these affect whether K/L codes apply or other special coding rules are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part K overall scope: bonds between heteroatoms (K1..K9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part K codes represent bonds between elements O, S, Se, Te, N, and halogen with main headings K1 (X=Y and X-Y bonds where X = halogen, Y = O,S,Se,Te,N,halogen), K2 (S=S and S-S), K3 (S=N and S-N), K4 (S=O and S-O), K5 (N:+N and N=N families), K6 (N-N), K7 (N=O), K8 (N-O), and K9 (O-O).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: some K codes are green on the coding sheet meaning searchable only from 1981/Week 27; valency and halogen identification rules apply (see specific K1..K9 notes). K1 notes: from 1978 forward the X atom is identified by a C0: halogen code; valency of halogen in K140 is coded C100/C200/C300; valency of S in K122 further specified by C116/C216. Unlike H/J/L codes, both atoms in K1 codes may be in the same ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: K2 notes: S=S and S-S bond coding nuances
rubrics_metrics.description: Set K2 covers S=S and S-S bonds with multiple subsets (K210..K299) indicating S=S, S-S, polysulfur etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: prior to 1970 K220 was not assigned to -S-S- groups containing SIV or SVI. Valency of S in Set K2 is coded via Part C for SIV (C216) and SVI (C316) unless K422 or K432 are also assigned. Prior to 1981 groups with SIV or SVI bonded solely to S or S and C were additionally coded in K4; since 1981 they are not. Fragments -S-S-S(=U)n- and -S-S(=U)n-S- (n=1 or 2) are coded K221, not K222+K299. Groups coded K223 are additionally coded in Part L: from 1981; prior to 1981 they were also assigned J2: precursor codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: K3 notes: S=N and S-N coding and valency assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Set K3 covers S=N and S-N bond types with multiple subsets (K310..K399).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups coded in K3 are additionally coded with valency codes C116 (SII), C216 (SIV), or C316 (SVI) depending on S valency; exception: -C#N=SII coded K310 with no additional valency code. Prior to 1981 amine sulphides were coded K742; since 1981 coded K320. Historical coding practices changed for S=N groups (previous broader assignments now replaced by precise definitions). Examples and cross-coding notes provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: K4 notes: S=O and S-O bond coding rules and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Set K4 covers S=O and S-O bonds with many specific subsets (K410..K499) indicating oxidation state, bonding patterns, ring membership, and polymeric occurrences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups with an S-X bond are additionally coded in K4 if they contain X-S(=T)n-T- (n = 0,1,2; at least one T is O). Groups with N-S or N=S bonds are not coded in K4 unless they contain at least one S-O or S=O and have certain fragments. Groups coded K410 may be additionally assigned codes K421..K433. K423, K433, K441, K442 are additionally coded C116/C216/C316 depending on S valency. K442 groups containing C=SIV or C=SVI are additionally coded L570. K431 is not assigned if the S atom is bonded to O, S, Se, Te, N, or halogen. K499 is only assigned when two or more S atoms are present and require the same K4 code repeatedly. Examples illustrate multi-code assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: K5-K9: additional K set notes (azo, N-N, N=O, N-O, O-O)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets K5..K9 cover azo and related N=N families, N-N bonds, N=O types, N-O bonds, and O-O bonds respectively, with subsets and poly options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes include cross-coding of azo dyes in Part W:, additional coding of N=N+= and -N+N in L72: from 1978 forward, historical/precursor code differences (1963-1981), and guidance on when K7/K8 codes should not be simultaneously assigned. K9: compounds coded K910 (-O-O- peroxide fragment) are additionally assigned a code for the group after removal of one O atom unless a specific code takes both O atoms into account. Prior to 1981 K999 was used differently; since 1981 K999 is assigned when any K9 code is applicable more than once.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part L: scope and general notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Part L codes cover various C–heteroatom combinations (O,S,Se,Te,N,halogen bonded to C), onium and free radical descriptors, sugars and derivatives, and groups that have more than one atom in the same ring; main headings include L1..L9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: Except for L710 and codes in L8 (sugars) and L9 (groups in rings), Part L codes are not applied if two or more adjacent atoms of the functional group are ring members—instead apply the code for the appropriate group with only one atom (or none) in the ring plus an appropriate L9 code. Heteroatom-to-metal and heteroatom-to-B/Si/P/As rules cross-referenced to Parts A and B. Symbol definitions (T,U,X,Y,W) for Part L provided. Quaternary ammonium (N+) compounds are coded in L72:; the parent amine receives applicable H-L codes except tertiary amine H103 is not assigned to ammonium; if N and all substituents are in same ring system parent amine is not coded. Examples and coding order rules given.
